feature_contract.goal: Complete the existing F11 interactive settings function while preserving Quest3 font readability, reliable edit/input ownership and the original game control fallback.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only the F11 external ImGui settings shell, its input forwarding and native Win32 keyboard/mouse fallback; no gameplay HUD, ESC renderer, FFB, SkyGlow or DX11 changes.
trace_stages: Original game Win32 WndprocHook receives keyboard, character and pointer messages
F11 overlay ImGui Win32 backend forwards events to the shell and editing controls
Overlay render and R30 screen-overlay binocular composition present F11, while dest_orig controls original game fallback
subcomponents: F11 shell and binding controls route keyboard, character, IME, pointer and wheel without forwarding duplicate input to game
Quest3 eye-density atlas and responsive shell layout preserve independently sized clickable ImGui controls
Hidden F11, clickable notifications, legacy toggle and OS shortcuts retain unmodified game/window behavior

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Visible F11 settings and binding dialogs receive key/IME/mouse/wheel events without a second original game WndProc input action.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Font atlas and binocular F11 presentation
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Current responsive font atlas and layout remain integrated with F11 input for gameplay and source-resolution resize, with HMD legibility reserved for real testing.
Closed F11 restores normal game input, notification pointer remains clickable and F11 toggle, focus events and Alt+F4 system shortcuts remain available.

acceptance_items.behavior_area: Windows DX9Ex source and OpenXR package
acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Exact SHA DX9Ex Active policy/game/host/full-chain/package, Domain, HUD and Full Source Impact checks succeed and the feature record is enforced fail-closed.

diagnosis.original_evidence: In WndprocHook::destination the original game dest_orig is called whenever ImGui_ImplWin32_WndProcHandler returns zero even for a forwarded key/click/wheel editing event.
source_trace: Original game WndprocHook receives message classes from Windows and maps F11 visibility and binding state.
ShouldForwardToImGui dispatches to ImGui_ImplWin32_WndProcHandler which may enqueue keyboard/mouse data yet return zero.
Before the repair, zero returned from that handler reaches original dest_orig and may also change game input while F11 is visibly active.
diagnosis.root_cause: ImGui backend event delivery and its return-value handling were conflated with ownership of game input, allowing UI-owned events to fall through to original WndProc.
alternatives_rejected: XR pixel density and F11 layout do not control Windows event-handler return semantics; R30 per-eye projection and SkyGlow are not touched.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: F11 source message classification and independent ShouldConsumeFromGame ownership decision added after ImGui dispatch, with legacy toggle/focus/system escape paths excluded.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Portable C++ static assertions, Python routing negative/mutation cases and fail-closed PowerShell feature-record runner guards.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: F11 remains an external ScreenOverlay2D ImGui composition, not an original game sprite; this edit changes only input ownership, not the already existing per-eye rendering transform.

runtime_evidence: OutRun2006 and Quest3/VDXR HMD gameplay were not exercised in this session. Functional and binocular correctness cannot be asserted.
controller_note: The first material SHA 6322fdca has a swallowed intermediate PowerShell policy error for a missing run record. This update supplies that record and makes every feature verifier exit fail-closed. Only a new exact SHA where all required Windows jobs pass is validation-bearing.
